mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares the properties of rectangles, rhombi, and squares?

options.A: A rectangle has all sides equal, a rhombus has all angles right, a square has opposite sides parallel.
options.B: A rectangle has opposite sides equal and all interior angles right; a rhombus has all sides equal; a square has both properties of a rectangle and a rhombus.
options.C: A rhombus always has right angles, while a rectangle never does; a square has only equal sides.
options.D: A rectangle and a rhombus are both types of squares.

mcqs.answer: A rectangle has opposite sides equal and all interior angles right; a rhombus has all sides equal; a square has both properties of a rectangle and a rhombus.
mcqs.explanation: A rectangle is defined by opposite sides being equal and all angles 90°. A rhombus is defined by all four sides being equal (angles need not be right). A square satisfies both definitions, having equal sides and right angles. Options A, C, and D contain incorrect statements.

mcqs.question: In the hierarchy of quadrilaterals, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Every square is a rectangle, but not every rectangle is a square.
options.B: Every rectangle is a rhombus, but not every rhombus is a rectangle.
options.C: Every rhombus is a square, but not every square is a rhombus.
options.D: Squares, rectangles, and rhombi are mutually exclusive categories.

mcqs.answer: Every square is a rectangle, but not every rectangle is a square.
mcqs.explanation: A square meets all the criteria of a rectangle (right angles and opposite sides equal) and also those of a rhombus (all sides equal). Hence every square is a rectangle, but a rectangle need not have equal sides, so it may not be a square. The other options reverse or deny these inclusion relationships.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a defining property of a rectangle?

options.B: Opposite sides are equal and all interior angles are 90°.
options.C: The diagonals are perpendicular to each other.
options.D: Only one pair of opposite sides is parallel.

mcqs.answer: Opposite sides are equal and all interior angles are 90°.
mcqs.explanation: A rectangle is a quadrilateral with opposite sides equal in length and each interior angle measuring 90 degrees. Option A describes a square or rhombus, C describes a kite or rhombus, and D describes a trapezium.

mcqs.question: Which property is always true for a rhombus?

options.B: The diagonals are equal in length.
options.D: Only one pair of sides is parallel.

mcqs.explanation: By definition, a rhombus has all four sides of equal length. Its angles need not be right angles, and its diagonals are generally unequal but bisect each other at right angles. Option D is false because a rhombus is a parallelogram, so both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines a square?

options.A: All sides are equal and all interior angles are 90°.
options.C: The diagonals are of different lengths.
options.D: It has exactly one right angle.

mcqs.answer: All sides are equal and all interior angles are 90°.
mcqs.explanation: A square combines the defining features of both a rectangle (right angles) and a rhombus (equal sides). Therefore it must have four equal sides and four right angles. The other options describe unrelated or incorrect properties.

mcqs.question: A quadrilateral has all four sides equal and one interior angle of 90°. Which special quadrilateral is it?
mcqs.explanation: Having all sides equal makes it a rhombus, and having a right angle makes it a rectangle. The only quadrilateral satisfying both conditions simultaneously is a square. A rectangle need not have equal sides, and a rhombus need not have right angles.

mcqs.question: A quadrilateral has opposite sides parallel and all interior angles equal to 90°. Which category does it belong to?
mcqs.explanation: Opposite sides being parallel makes it a parallelogram; the additional condition that all angles are 90° upgrades it to a rectangle. It is not necessarily a rhombus because side lengths are not specified as equal, and a trapezium has only one pair of parallel sides.

mcqs.question: A garden is shaped as a rectangle with length 12 m and width 8 m. Which property guarantees that the two longer sides are equal in length?
mcqs.explanation: In a rectangle, each pair of opposite sides are equal; therefore the two longer sides (the length) are equal to each other. Option A describes a square, C is not a property of rectangles, and D alone does not ensure side equality.
